question:
Choose the idiom/phrase that can substitute the highlighted group of words meaningfully.

She is **listening with full attention** whenever there is a mention of her favourite hero.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"All ears"** means listening very attentively. (पूरी तरह से सुनना)

 
 
• **Example: **Whenever the teacher talks about space exploration, the students are **all ears.**
 
 
 
• **"Full attention" **refers to focusing completely on something or someone. (पूरा ध्यान)
 
 
• **Example: **During the meeting, she gave her** full attention** to the speaker.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the phrase **"all ears" can be used to describe someone who is listening with full attention.**

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Beat around the bush **(घुमा फिरा कर बात करना): To avoid getting to the point or the main topic.

 
 
• **Example:** Stop beating around the bush and tell me what you want.
 
 
 
• **Run out of steam **(थक जाना): To lose energy or enthusiasm.
 
 
• **Example: **After working non-stop for hours, I ran out of steam and needed a break.
 
 
 
• **Break a leg** (शुभकामनाएँ): A way to wish someone good luck, especially before a performance.
 
 
• **Example:** Before the play began, everyone told the actors to break a leg.
